tier_reason: First-party numbers from the authors' own harness: bench/ua-vs-human/run.pl and ciphers/des/compile.pl (master branch) with SUPERCOP give code, compilers and flags (clang/icc -O3 with -march=native or ISA flags) for Usuba against hand-tuned references, but no CPU model is stated anywhere in the repo, so not A; the PLDI 2019 paper could not be opened (irif.fr, HAL and dariusmercadier.com unreachable) and its abstract, seen only in a search snippet, says 'on par', so it cannot lift the tier to B.

corrections.baseline: Hand-tuned reference implementations in SUPERCOP, compiled with the same C compilers at -O3: Kwan's bitsliced DES (C), Kasper-Schwabe SSSE3 AES-CTR and Kivilinna's AVX AES-CTR (assembly), Dolbeau AVX2, moon AVX/SSSE3 and e/ref ChaCha20, Linux C and avx2-16way/avx-8way/sse2-8way Serpent-CTR, and the Rectangle reference. Secondary: BSC 0.1 (Thomas Pornin's prototype bitslicing compiler, which emits C) on DES in results.org.
corrections.claimed_speedup: bench/ua-vs-human/human.tex (cycles per byte; SUPERCOP xor_cycles on 4096-byte messages, lower half of samples averaged; speedup = (ref - usuba)/ref). Usuba faster: Rectangle SSE 11.18 vs 14.51 (+22.95%), AVX 4.21 vs 4.92 (+14.43%), AVX2 2.10 vs 2.45 (+14.29%), GP 25.88 vs 28.61 (+9.54%); Serpent GP 25.78 vs 30.37 Linux C (+15.11%), SSE 11.29 vs 11.48 (+1.66%); ChaCha20 SSE 2.31 vs 2.72 moon SSSE3 (+15.07%), AVX2 1.02 vs 1.03, AVX 2.07 vs 2.09; DES GP 11.47 vs 12.01 Kwan (+4.50%). Usuba slower: AES 7.92 vs 7.77 Kasper-Schwabe (-1.93%) and 5.71 vs 5.59 Kivilinna AVX assembly (-2.15%); Serpent AVX2 4.53 vs 4.33 (-4.62%) and AVX 8.66 vs 8.36 (-3.59%); ChaCha20 GP 5.65 vs 5.64. ciphers/des/results.txt also has Usuba behind Kwan on SSE (6.64 vs 6.50) and AVX (3.74 vs 3.63). results.org (main branch): des-usuba 17.086 +-0.121 vs des-bsc 17.419 +-0.142 cycles/byte, about 1.9 percent faster (derived from page data). PLDI 2019 abstract: 'on par with hand-tuned reference implementations' (search snippet only); WPMVP 2018 quoted as about 15 percent faster on DES with 64-bit general-purpose registers depending on the C compiler (search snippet only).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Usuba emits C that is compiled by the same C compilers as the references. DES (ciphers/des/compile.pl): clang -O3 -march=native for both Usuba and Kwan. SUPERCOP rows (bench/ua-vs-human/run.pl): icc or clang with -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -fwrapv -std=gnu11 plus -march=native, -mssse3, -xSSSE3, -xSSE2 or -msse4.2; several rows pair different compilers or ISA flags per side (Serpent GP: Usuba clang -march=native vs Linux C icc -msse4.2; Serpent AVX: Usuba clang vs reference icc; ChaCha20 GP: Usuba icc -msse4.2 vs e/ref icc -march=native). usuba-vs-bsc (experimentations/usuba-vs-bsc/run.pl): clang -O3 -Wall -Wextra for both, Usuba flags -no-arr -inline-all -no-precalc-tbl -check-tbl -B. Compiler versions not stated.
corrections.hardware: Not stated; SUPERCOP data paths name an amd64 host 'dadaubuntu', CPU model unknown.
corrections.workload: Usuba-generated bitsliced or m-sliced ciphers (DES, AES-CTR, ChaCha20, Serpent-CTR, Rectangle) against hand-tuned references in SUPERCOP crypto_stream (xor_cycles over 4096-byte messages), plus bitsliced DES generated by Usuba against DES generated by BSC 0.1 in experimentations/usuba-vs-bsc (rdtscp cycles per byte, 15 runs).
corrections.caveats: Win is mixed and small: faster on Rectangle (9.5-23%), Serpent GP (15%), ChaCha20 SSE (15%) and DES GP (4.5%); slower on AES (about 2%), Serpent AVX/AVX2 (3.6-4.6%) and DES SSE/AVX; the paper itself claims 'on par'. The results.org DES comparison is against BSC 0.1, which the experiment's own Readme calls a prototype 'not meant to be an optimizing compiler', so it is not a hand-tuned baseline. The hand-tuned comparison lives only on the old master branch (bench/ua-vs-human/human.tex, ciphers/des/results.txt); the default main branch was restructured and no longer carries bench/, ciphers/ or experimentations/. Numbers are undated author runs on an unstated CPU, and some rows use different compilers or ISA flags for each side. Usuba output is C compiled by the same C compiler, so the gain comes from the Usubac compiler's transformations (scheduling, interleaving, inlining), not from a different backend. results.org also logs broken runs ('No supercop', 'C compilation goes wrong', a stack overflow, 0.00 AVX-512 results). Papers not opened (snippet only).
corrections.why_faster: Usubac transformations on the emitted C: bitslice-aware instruction scheduling (bench/scheduling-bs), interleaving of independent cipher instances (bench/interleaving: serpent-inter 25.84 vs serpent 34.13 cycles), aggressive inlining, and choice of bitslicing or m-slicing per target; the usuba-vs-bsc Readme credits Usuba's optimizations, not the language.

notes: Real data point, tier C kept. Record's baseline was wrong: 'bsc' is Pornin's non-optimizing prototype bitslicing compiler, not hand-tuned C; the hand-tuned comparison is bench/ua-vs-human/human.tex on the master branch (benchmark_url corrected), which shows Usuba ahead on Rectangle, Serpent GP, ChaCha20 SSE and DES GP and behind on AES and Serpent AVX/AVX2. Shortcomings to record: claim is 'on par' with mixed wins, CPU model unstated, some rows use different compilers per side, master-branch-only data, papers unreachable (snippet only), repo stale since 2024-09-04.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: actix: rust:1.94 image, RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo build --release with release profile opt-level=3, codegen-units=1, lto='thin', panic='abort'; actix-web pinned to unreleased git rev 67490f9e, rustls 0.23 with ring for TLS (frameworks/actix/Dockerfile, Cargo.toml). Drogon: unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image, app built with CMake Release (C++20), libjemalloc preloaded, no -march=native or LTO (frameworks/drogon). Cutelyst: CMake Release. nginx 1.31.4: -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG with a custom C handler module. h2o: clang Release with -march=native -mtune=native, no LTO.
corrections.caveats: Mixed against C and C++ on the same board. At baseline-4096 actix (2,775,120) beats only Drogon (2,022,710) and Cutelyst (2,153,860) among nine C/C++ entries; it trails nginx 3,284,513, h2o 3,641,609, mongoose 3,707,598, agensio (C++) 3,558,559, hical (C++) 3,228,043, libreactorng 4,377,377 and libioma 4,255,834. At limited-conn-4096 it is behind Drogon and Cutelyst too (1,135,157 vs 1,694,883 and 1,736,401) and far behind nginx 2,626,297. json-tls: 1,157,219 vs nginx 1,313,755, h2o 1,229,462 and agensio 1,716,076 (ahead of Drogon 253,055 and mongoose 1,102,964). static-tls 55,882 and static-h2 51,989-64,019 vs nginx 720,869 and 796,607-802,090. Wins over Drogon also on json-comp (541,211 vs 127,466, where Drogon's jsoncpp allocation churn dominates), async-32000 (Drogon entry runs every delay timer on one loop, per wave 5) and fixed-rate CPU per request (latency-1m 24.9 vs 32.1 us). pipelined-4096 (16,338,425 vs Drogon 7,801,404 and nginx 4,037,345) is a reference-only profile excluded from HttpArena's composite score. actix.json still carries baseline-h2c/json-h2c rows although actix's meta.json no longer subscribes to them (stale). Rows come from separate runs on the same machine (actix last saved 2026-09-06, Drogon 2026-09-06, nginx 2026-08-30); the actix entry runs an unreleased actix-web git revision; Drogon is built from an unpinned image without -march=native while actix gets target-cpu=native and thin LTO; handlers are minimal (nginx is a custom C module). Third-party swerver-benchmarks (Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon, 2 CPUs) has actix 133,691 vs nginx 118,061 req/s, while statico's README has nginx ahead (832,082 vs 798,809 at four threads, 286,960 vs 213,756 at one).
corrections.why_faster: Not established by the sources. Same event-loop-per-core design as Drogon's trantor; the gap reflects framework implementation (HTTP parsing, routing, response building, and serde_json vs jsoncpp on JSON rows) rather than a Rust language effect.

notes: Tier upgraded to A (CPU model is published in HttpArena's current.json and hardware docs); all quoted numbers verified. Shortcomings to record: beats only Drogon and Cutelyst of nine C/C++ entries at baseline-4096 and loses to both at limited-conn-4096; behind nginx on the scored H/1.1, TLS and static profiles; pipelined win is reference-only; Drogon built without -march=native/LTO from an unpinned image; framework-vs-framework, not a language-level win.

corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (Zen 2, 64 cores / 128 threads, single NUMA node), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.17.0-22, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), performance governor (site/data/current.json; site/content/docs/hardware/_index.md). corrections.compiler_and_flags: cardigan 0.1.0-alpha.5: maven eclipse-temurin JDK 26 build, eclipse-temurin:26-jre runtime with --enable-preview --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED --add-modules jdk.incubator.vector -Xms512m -Xmx2g -XX:MaxInlineSize=150 -XX:FreqInlineSize=600 (frameworks/cardigan/Dockerfile); TLS through the system libssl.so.3/libcrypto.so.3 via Panama with opportunistic kTLS. nginx 1.31.4: -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG with a custom C handler module, worker_processes auto, reuseport. Drogon: CMake Release with jemalloc preloaded. h2o: clang Release -march=native -mtune=native, no LTO.
corrections.caveats: The win over nginx is architectural (io_uring thread-per-core vs nginx's epoll workers), not Java: the io_uring C engines on the same board beat cardigan at baseline-4096 (libreactorng 4,377,377, libioma 4,255,834 vs 3,947,346), and at limited-conn-4096 cardigan (2,613,832) is behind nginx 2,626,297, h2o 2,651,569, libreactorng 2,685,717, mongoose 2,701,933 and libioma 2,707,029. On h2/h2c nginx is the outlier: h2o leads baseline-h2-256 (16,106,978 vs 14,467,569) and agensio (C++) leads baseline-h2-256 (14,744,015) and h2c-256 (15,185,367 vs 15,144,652), so the 4.2x and 6.2x ratios measure nginx's HTTP/2 stack. TLS rows (baseline-h2, json-tls 1,703,461 vs nginx 1,313,755 and agensio 1,716,076) run OpenSSL 3 through Panama FFI with kTLS, so crypto is C or kernel code. pipelined-4096 (45,708,428 vs nginx 4,037,345; libreactorng 43,424,448) is a reference-only profile excluded from the composite score. Fixed-rate CPU per request is mixed (latency-1m 20.4 us, second only to libioma 19.3; latency-10k 31.7 us, behind most C/C++ entries; 8gbit 60.7 vs mongoose 57.4 and Drogon 58.3). Experimental alpha (0.1.0-alpha.5, 28 commits, 1 star), relies on unsupported JDK internals (APOLOGY.md), needs JDK 26 preview and incubator Vector API and Linux 6.1+. The entry was contributed by the cardigan author; rows come from separate runs on the same machine (cardigan last saved 2026-09-03, nginx 2026-08-30); the repo README states no benchmark numbers; handlers are minimal (nginx is a custom C module).
corrections.why_faster: Thread-per-core, shared-nothing event loops driving io_uring directly through Panama (pinned carrier threads, multishot and fixed-file operations) against nginx's epoll workers, plus OpenSSL with kTLS transmit offload on TLS rows; the C io_uring engines on the same board are faster still, so the gain is the I/O architecture, not the Java language.

notes: Tier upgraded to A (HttpArena publishes the CPU model); all quoted numbers verified. Shortcomings to record: not a language win (C io_uring engines libreactorng and libioma beat it at baseline-4096; behind every C engine at limited-conn-4096), h2/h2c ratios reflect a slow nginx HTTP/2 stack (h2o and agensio level or ahead), TLS crypto is OpenSSL/kTLS via FFI, pipelined is reference-only, experimental alpha with 1 star and unsupported JDK internals.
